title: SMC Single Candle Order Block (SCOB) Entry Technique

swing_point_foundation.llm_summary: Before understanding Single Candle Order Block (SCOB), one must understand swing points at the candlestick level. A swing point forms from a minimum of 3 candles: the middle candle sweeps the previous candle's liquidity (high or low), and the third candle closes beyond the middle candle's opposite extreme. Two types: (1) High Swing Point — middle candle sweeps (or closes above) previous candle's high liquidity, third candle closes below middle candle's low. The middle candle's HIGH must remain protected (price should not return above it). (2) Low Swing Point — middle candle sweeps (or closes below) previous candle's low, third candle closes above middle candle's high. The middle candle's LOW must remain protected. Candle colors do NOT matter — only the pattern (sweep + opposite close + protected extreme).
key_rules: Swing point = minimum 3-candle pattern
Middle candle sweeps previous candle's liquidity (high or low)
Third candle closes beyond middle candle's opposite extreme
High Swing Point: middle candle sweeps previous high → third candle closes below middle candle's low
Low Swing Point: middle candle sweeps previous low → third candle closes above middle candle's high
Middle candle's extreme (high for High SP, low for Low SP) MUST remain protected
Protected = price does not return beyond that extreme
Candle colors do NOT matter — only the pattern matters
Two sweep types: wick sweep (sweep and close inside) or body close beyond (stronger)

scob_definition.llm_summary: Single Candle Order Block (SCOB), also called SCOOP, is an entry confirmation technique based on swing points. The middle candle of a valid swing point IS the SCOB candle. SCOB is used at Point of Interest (POI) zones for precise entry: FVG (1st priority), IOF/Institutional Order Flow (2nd priority), Order Block (3rd priority), or at any liquidity sweep of a previous high/low. Bullish SCOB: middle candle sweeps previous candle's low → next candle closes above middle candle's high → the middle candle is the bullish SCOB. Bearish SCOB: middle candle sweeps previous candle's high → next candle closes below middle candle's low → the middle candle is the bearish SCOB. The SCOB candle is only valid when it forms at a significant level — a previous high/low liquidity sweep, FVG rejection, or order block rejection.
key_rules: SCOB (Single Candle Order Block) = entry confirmation technique based on swing points
Also called SCOOP (Single Candle Order Block)
The MIDDLE candle of a valid swing point = the SCOB candle
Bullish SCOB: middle candle sweeps previous low → next candle closes above middle high
Bearish SCOB: middle candle sweeps previous high → next candle closes below middle low
SCOB ONLY valid when forming at significant level (previous high/low sweep, FVG, OB)
POI zone priority for SCOB: FVG (1st) → IOF Candle (2nd) → Order Block (3rd)
SCOB can also form at liquidity sweep of any previous high/low
Entry: at SCOB candle's retest | SL: beyond SCOB candle's extreme | TP: previous structure low/high

scob_types_and_variations.llm_summary: SCOB can consist of 3 to 5 candles depending on conditions. Standard SCOB (3 candles): middle candle sweeps previous candle's liquidity, third candle closes beyond middle candle's opposite extreme — the blue/middle candle is marked as SCOB. Extended SCOB (4 candles): middle candle sweeps liquidity but third candle fails to close beyond the opposite extreme — wait for fourth candle. If fourth candle closes beyond, the candle that swept the liquidity is still the SCOB. Inside candle variation: if the third candle is an inside candle (doesn't sweep previous candle's liquidity), and fourth candle breaks both candles' extreme, skip the inside candle and mark the first sweeping candle as SCOB. High Probability SCOB: when a Fair Value Gap (FVG) exists immediately below (bearish) or above (bullish) the SCOB candle. The FVG adds confluence and provides better risk-to-reward. The bottom row of the diagram shows all 4 standard patterns repeated with FVG zones underneath each SCOB, making them 'High Probability SCOB' entries.
key_rules: Standard SCOB = 3 candles (middle sweeps, third closes beyond)
Extended SCOB = 4-5 candles (third candle fails to close → wait for fourth)
Inside candle variation: skip inside candle → mark the first sweeping candle as SCOB
High Probability SCOB: FVG exists immediately below/above the SCOB candle
FVG below bearish SCOB = high probability (better risk/reward)
FVG above bullish SCOB = high probability (better risk/reward)
Without FVG: SCOB is still valid but lower probability
4 standard bearish SCOB patterns + 4 high probability versions with FVG

where_to_trade_scob.llm_summary: SCOB should be found and traded at specific locations in the market structure. In a bearish trend: (1) identify the first valid pullback (inducement), (2) mark the sell zone above the inducement, (3) when market approaches the sell zone — look for SCOB formation at the rejection. The SCOB forms when market taps the sell zone and creates a swing point rejection (middle candle sweeps the zone's liquidity, next candle drops). If the SCOB has FVG immediately below it → high probability. On the same timeframe (e.g., M15): first priority is SCOB on the trading timeframe itself. Can also refine to lower TF (M5) to find FVG inside the SCOB candle. For secondary entry: when market creates recent/minor inducement (internal structure IDM) without reaching the main sell zone, look for SCOB at that inducement sweep. When a sell/buy zone has engineered liquidity or inducement nearby → the zone becomes very high probability → can take direct entry at the zone even without waiting for SCOB. Take profit = the low from which market rallied to the zone (where market moved up from).
key_rules: Trade SCOB at sell/buy zones above/below inducement
Bearish: identify IDM → mark sell zone above IDM → wait for SCOB at rejection
First priority: SCOB on the trading timeframe itself (e.g., M15 SCOB on M15 chart)
Can refine: drop to M5 to find FVG inside the M15 SCOB candle
When zone has engineered liquidity/IDM nearby → very high probability → direct entry OK
SCOB entry: at SCOB candle retest | SL: 1-2 pips beyond SCOB extreme | TP: previous structure low/high
Take profit = the low/high from which market rallied/dropped to the zone
Unmitigated SCOB zones can be used for future trades
Internal IDM sweep + SCOB = valid secondary entry without needing HTF zone tap

real_chart_scob_application.llm_summary: Complete real-chart demonstration on EUR/USD M15: (1) Market is bearish on M15. (2) Market takes out major inducement and drops → structure shift confirmed. (3) Internal structure creates minor inducement. (4) Sell zone marked at FVG above the internal inducement. (5) First SCOB identified: candle sweeps the internal inducement → next candle drops aggressively below the SCOB candle's low → SCOB confirmed. (6) Refine to M5: inside the M15 SCOB candle, 3 aggressive red candles with internal FVG visible → high probability SCOB. (7) Entry at SCOB retest → SL above SCOB candle → TP at previous low → first take profit HIT. (8) The unmitigated FVG zone remains valid for future. (9) Market creates engineered liquidity (equal tops/double top) near the FVG → very high probability zone. (10) Second entry: direct entry at the FVG zone (because engineered liquidity nearby provides extra confluence) → strong drop → 1:5 to 1:6 risk/reward achieved. Key insight: when zone has nearby engineered liquidity/inducement → you can take direct entry without waiting for SCOB.
key_rules: Real example: EUR/USD M15 bearish SCOB trade
Step 1: Confirm bearish M15 trend + major IDM taken + structure shift
Step 2: Mark internal IDM and sell zones (FVG above IDM)
Step 3: Identify SCOB at internal IDM sweep → candle sweeps IDM, next closes below
Step 4: Refine to M5 → find FVG inside M15 SCOB → high probability confirmation
Step 5: Entry at SCOB retest → SL above SCOB → TP at previous low
Unmitigated zones remain valid for future trades
Equal tops / double tops near zone = engineered liquidity → very high probability
Zone with nearby engineered liquidity → direct entry OK → 1:5 to 1:6 R:R achievable
SMC rule: market rallies from a low to reach zone → that low = first take profit target
